Agent interoperability protocols and standards — MCP (Model Context Protocol), A2A (Agent-to-Agent), tool-use / function-calling standards, OpenTelemetry for AI, agent runtime standards

news_collector._priority_vendors_comment: Frontier labs whose announcements must NEVER be missed. The news skill treats these as mandatory coverage: every URL fetched, fallback_search invoked if the index page is egress-blocked, vendor permalink preferred over aggregator coverage in synthesis. Edit freely — this is just a list, no other config depends on the keys.

openai.fallback_search: site:openai.com 2026 announcement OR release OR launch

anthropic._comment: Anthropic publishes across TWO domains: anthropic.com/news (corporate/policy/partnerships) and claude.com/blog (product announcements — Claude apps, Claude Code, MCP server features). Both must be watched. Gap noticed 2026-05-12 when Claude Code agent-view announcement was cited via root index instead of canonical claude.com/blog/agent-view-in-claude-code URL.
anthropic.fallback_search: (site:anthropic.com OR site:claude.com) 2026 (announcement OR release OR launch OR enterprise OR agents OR Claude-Code)

deepseek.fallback_search: DeepSeek 2026 (V4 OR R2 OR release OR announcement) site:huggingface.co OR site:x.com

news_collector._enterprise_vendors_comment: Enterprise AI platforms — the layer ABOVE frontier-lab announcements. These are the vendors who package frontier models for the enterprise market (SAP, Salesforce, ServiceNow), the ones who own enterprise infra (Red Hat, IBM, NVIDIA, Snowflake, Databricks), and the workflow/automation layer that's becoming AI-native (n8n, Workday). Same coverage discipline as priority_vendors: every URL fetched, fallback_search invoked if egress-blocked, vendor permalink preferred over aggregator. Without this section the digest skewed toward frontier-lab MCP/A2A chatter and missed major business news (n8n becoming Germany's most valuable AI co via SAP deal, Red Hat AI 3.4 release, etc.).

linkedin_collector.comment_priority: topic_over_author — substantive content wins regardless of poster's follower count or title
feeds_to_scan: Pulse search via Google: site:linkedin.com/pulse {topic} (one query per pulse_topic_queries entry, last 14 days)
Pulse search via LinkedIn content search (sortBy=date_posted, datePosted=past-week) for each focus_areas topic
linkedin_collector.url_capture_rule: Captured link must match /pulse/, /posts/, or /feed/update/{urn}. Search-result URLs and bare /feed/ URLs are NOT acceptable — drop the item if you cannot extract a canonical post URL.
linkedin_collector.note: Auto-enabled when Chrome is reachable; silent skip otherwise. Topic-driven Pulse search is the priority layer; hashtag and home-feed scans are secondary.

weekly_digest.output_format: tight summary with links into source dailies

radar_config._comment: Trend radar — fired daily by orchestrator after daily synthesis. Scores topics by source-weighted convergence over a rolling window; smooths via EMA to avoid daily jumps. Outputs radar/{date}.md (human-read) + radar/{date}.json (structured data for future web app). Tune the constants here; the SKILL reads them at runtime.
radar_config._ema_comment: Two EMAs run in parallel. Fast (α=0.3, ~2.3-day half-life) reacts to news of the day. Slow (α=0.05, ~14-day half-life) tracks structural shifts. Stage classification uses score_slow so loud single events don't bounce topics between stages — fast vs. slow comparison tells you direction. score_fast > score_slow → rising; score_fast < score_slow → fading. Tune 'ema_alpha_slow' lower (e.g., 0.02 → ~35-day half-life) if the radar still feels too event-driven; tune higher (e.g., 0.1 → ~7-day) if it feels too slow to react.

source_weights._comment: Per-mention contribution. Higher = stronger signal. Tune by raising weights for sources you trust more.

convergence_multiplier._comment: When a topic appears in N or more DIFFERENT source types, score is multiplied. Counters monoculture (single-source loud day) and rewards cross-source agreement.

max_mentions_per_source_type._comment: Per-source cap on counted mentions per topic per run. Prevents one chatty source (LinkedIn hashtags, Medium aggregators) from dominating the score just by volume. Beyond the cap, additional mentions are recorded in source_mentions for transparency but stop adding to raw_score. Tune up/down based on what dominates the radar — added 2026-05-12 after LinkedIn accounted for 46% of a topic's score.

stages._comment: Each topic falls into one stage based on score AND sustained signal. Tuning these thresholds shifts how aggressively the radar promotes/demotes themes.

emerging.description: Early signal. 1-2 weak sources or one strong novel source. Worth watching.

consolidating.description: Multiple independent sources are converging on the same take. Pattern is forming.

mainstream.description: Consensus. Most credible sources reference this; further coverage is incremental.

fading._trigger: score declined >25% over rolling window AND was previously >=50
fading.description: Was hot, now declining. Useful to know — don't bet here, expect coverage to dry up.

topic_taxonomy_seed._comment: Seed list of known topics so the radar has stable IDs across days. The group keys (frontier_models, agent_protocols, etc.) are CATEGORY HINTS — they bias initial clustering but are NOT authoritative. Each run's sectors are determined dynamically by the radar skill from the topics that are actually active that week. The field evolves: RAG was a sector once; today its topics scatter across Agents and Retrieval. Agent may add new topic IDs as new themes appear.

sector_config._comment: Dynamic sectors (radar quadrants) — recomputed every run based on what's actually active. Sectors carry over from yesterday's radar unless hysteresis rules trigger a change. This is what makes it a TREND radar (sectors evolve) rather than a fixed taxonomy. User-stated reason 2026-05-14: 'if I had this earlier, we had only Models / RAG, and now from RAG we went to Agents, that's why I say it needs to be flexible.'
sector_config._clustering_method: LLM clusters topics into themes by reading topic labels + supporting context. Prior run's sectors are passed in as starting point — clusterer keeps them when membership is stable, splits/merges/renames only when warranted. The topic_taxonomy_seed group keys above are initial hints, NOT enforced labels.
sector_config._starter_sectors_comment: Used only on the very first radar run when no prior sectors exist. After that, the clusterer evolves them. If sectors get stuck for too long, manually clearing prior_sectors in the most recent radar JSON forces a fresh cluster.

breadth_config._comment: Cross-source breadth — orthogonal to the EMA-based persistence score. Answers 'how many distinct organizations are talking about this right now?' as a primary, visible dimension. User-stated reason 2026-05-14: 'if many companies are talking or writing about the same topic, this means high-weighted related, should be seen easier.'
breadth_config._org_definition: An 'org' is the primary publisher or subject of the mention — Anthropic, OpenAI, ServiceNow, Heise, Handelsblatt, an individual author of a long-form blog post. The radar skill extracts orgs from each mention's context. For backfill where org data isn't separately stored, breadth is approximated by distinct (source_type, file_date) pairs in the window.

thresholds._comment: How the viewer interprets breadth into visual cues.

output_format.primary_view: radar.md — human read, narrative with stage groupings
output_format.machine_view: radar.json — structured data for future visualization (Angular / HTML / Streamlit / etc.)
